title: 史記 卷一百二十三 大宛列傳 (Shiji ch. 123, Zhang Qian's report: Daxia and Shendu)
quote: 臣在大夏時，見邛竹杖、蜀布
summary: Zhang Qian reports that in Daxia (Bactria) he saw bamboo canes of Qiong and cloth of Shu (Sichuan); Daxia people said their merchants bought them in Shendu (India), several thousand li south-east. On this inference he argues for a route to Daxia via Shu.

ask_addressed: Quote Chinese primary sources for contact and transmission along the Silk Road, from an opened edition or translation (ctext.org, archive.org, Wikisource): Shiji ch. 123 (Sima Qian on Zhang Qian's mission and Dayuan, Daxia/Bactria), Hou Hanshu on the Prince of Chu Ying (65 CE) and the first imperial reference to the Buddha, Hou Hanshu on Cai Lun and paper (105 CE), and the Record of Buddhist Kingdoms (Faxian, c. 414 CE) or Xuanzang's Records.
title: Shiji (Wikipedia), textual history
quote: Only two fragments of pre-Tang dynasty Shiji manuscripts have survived
summary: The page records that only two pre-Tang Shiji fragments survive and that the earliest extant copy dates to 420-589; the Shiji also received later additions.
limits: Basis for the composition range and witness fields above; tertiary.
